steps.note: Start a multi-stage event creation flow for the RFQ.
Ensure RFQ counter offers are available for the buyer.
Provide the required event title.
Create an RFQ pricing stage, which is the subject of the counter offer.
Apply the RFQ pricing template before adding products.
Add the line item whose original quote will be countered.
Populate the RFQ pricing sheet.
Commit a bidding schedule so the event can be published.
Invite both named vendors so Vendor A can receive the counter offer and Vendor B can be checked separately.
Publish the event before bidding.
Confirm the event reached a real published project page.
Confirm Vendor A's bid was accepted.
the test asks the vendor to bid for themselves
Confirm the second vendor response was accepted.
Open the buyer comparison grid containing both bids before sending the counter offer.
Send Vendor A the required counter price and remark.
Confirm the buyer grid marks the counter offer as initiated for Vendor A.
Switch to Vendor A's separate supplier-portal session.
Open the event overview where the pending counter offer notice is shown.
Verify the notice includes Vendor A's original quoted price.
Verify the notice includes the buyer's offered counter price.
Verify the buyer's counter-offer remark is displayed.
Verify Vendor A can accept the pending counter offer.
Verify the vendor view exposes the rejection action, using the case's expected label.
